subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & success criteria
message_1_subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & success criteria
message_1_body:
Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment on goals. Quick recap and next steps for the POC we discussed:

- Goal: Demonstrate that Redwood can achieve production-quality intent classification and routing for ACME's customer support flows while meeting latency and hallucination SLOs.
- Success criteria (draft): accuracy >= 85% on ACME-labeled test set; hallucination rate < 2% on representative queries; P95 latency < 450ms in Dedicated environment; no critical security gaps for SOC2 controls.
- Proposed eval approach: start with an offline evaluation on your labeled set + curated challenge cases, then run a 2-week online shadow in pre-prod to capture latency, throughput, and real-world failure modes.
- Ownership: ACME provides labeled test set, priority intents, and data mapping. Redwood provides the infra, eval harness, and initial rubric (attached).
- Timeline (draft): Week 0: onboarding & access; Week 1: offline eval and tuning; Weeks 2-3: online shadow and metric collection; Week 4: review & decision.

I've attached the evaluation plan and a sample grading rubric for your review. Please confirm: 1) that the success criteria look reasonable, 2) whether you can share an anonymized labeled sample (or a mapping document), and 3) whether ACME is comfortable with a 2-week shadow run (we can do longer if you'd prefer).

Next step: can we lock in a kickoff on Monday (June 7) for onboarding?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: acme_poc_evaluation_plan_v1.pdf, acme_evals_rubric_v1.xlsx
message_2_subject: Re: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & success criteria
message_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few quick clarifying questions before we confirm kickoff:

1) Offline eval vs online shadow: can you outline the minimum data format you need for the offline eval (columns, expected labels)? We have PII concerns so we may need to provide an anonymized subset.
2) For the online shadow: can Redwood run the shadow in our pre-prod (not prod) and capture metrics? Will there be any routing or opt-in required from our side?
3) Security: our InfoSec will want to see the SOC2 controls and a short data flow diagram. We plan to run this through procurement.

Also, would you be open to shortening the shadow to 1 week for an initial sanity check and then extend to 2 weeks if metrics look good?

Cc'ing Nina (product lead) — Nina, any concerns on the success criteria above?

Best,
Samir
Director, AI Platform — ACME Corp
message_3_subject: Re: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & success criteria
message_3_body:
Thanks Samir — great questions. Proposed answers and a refined plan below:

1) Offline eval data format:
- Minimum: CSV with columns [request_id, text, gold_label, timestamp]. Optional: intent confidence, metadata (channel, locale). If PII is a concern, an anonymized sample (remove PII fields) works fine — we just need representative examples per intent.

2) Online shadow in pre-prod:
- Yes — we can run the shadow in your pre-prod environment. Routing is non-invasive: requests are forked to Redwood for inference but continue to your prod endpoint. No customer-visible routing change required. We will not write back to your production systems unless you ask us to.

3) Security/compliance:
- We'll share our SOC2 summary and a short data flow diagram with procurement. I'll surface the security questionnaire link below.

4) Hybrid eval approach (recommended):
- Week 0 (kickoff): access, onboarding, and sample dataset ingestion.
- Week 1 (offline): run the offline eval against your labeled sample + curated challenge cases. Deliver a preliminary accuracy/hallucination report.
- Week 2 (shadow start): 1 week of online shadow (sanity run) to validate latency and basic throughput metrics.
- Week 3 (shadow extended): optional extra week to collect more edge cases if Week 2 shows issues.
- Week 4: wrap-up call to review metrics and determine go/no-go.

5) Grading rubric (summary):
- Accuracy (weighted 40%): correct intent classification on labeled set. Target >= 85%.
- Relevance/precision (weighted 20%): responses are on-topic and actionable.
- Hallucination rate (weighted 15%): percent of responses with fabricated facts; target < 2%.
- Latency (weighted 15%): P95 latency under 450ms.
- Operational stability (weighted 10%): error rate, timeouts, resource usage.

If ACME is comfortable, we can do a 1-week initial shadow and extend to 2 weeks based on early signals. I'll attach an updated evaluation plan and rubric (attached) and link the HubSpot record for tracking.

Action items for ACME: share an anonymized labeled sample (or mapping doc) and confirm whether procurement wants the SOC2 summary now. Proposed kickoff: Monday, June 7 — does that still work?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_poc_evaluation_plan_v1.pdf, acme_evals_rubric_v1.xlsx
